content: If someone has taken too much linezolid, seek medical attention immediately. Call 911 or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose of linezolid, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. It is crucial to complete the entire prescribed course of linezolid, even if your symptoms improve or resolve, to reduce the risk of future infections becoming resistant to linezolid or similar medications. The most common side effects of linezolid include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, and anemia. Inform your healthcare provider if any of these side effects bother you. There may be other side effects not listed here, so contact your healthcare provider if you suspect you are experiencing a side effect. You can also report side effects to the FDA at 800-FDA-1088 or Health Canada at 866-234-2345. Serious side effects of linezolid include: 1. Severe Allergic Reactions: Stop using linezolid and seek immediate medical help if you experience breathing difficulties, wheezing, swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat, trouble swallowing, throat tightness, itching, skin rash, or hives. 2. Decreased Blood Cells (Myelosuppression): Linezolid can suppress bone marrow function, leading to reduced blood cell production. 3. Serotonin Syndrome: Linezolid increases serotonin levels, and when combined with certain medications, it can cause serotonin syndrome. Symptoms include confusion, agitation, headache, fever, sweating, abnormal heartbeat, muscle twitching, stiffness, shivering, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Seek emergency help if these occur. 4. Nerve Problems: Linezolid may cause peripheral neuropathy (nerve damage) or optic neuropathy (nerve damage affecting the eyes). Stop taking linezolid and contact your healthcare provider if you experience vision changes, pain, burning, tingling, numbness, or weakness in your arms, hands, legs, or feet. 5. Seizures: Some individuals taking linezolid have reported seizures. Symptoms may include muscle twitching, jerking, spasms, tremors, stiffening of the arms and legs, anxiety, confusion, dizziness, or loss of consciousness. Stop taking linezolid and contact your healthcare provider if you experience these symptoms. 6. Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea: Overgrowth of Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) in the gut can occur with antibiotics like linezolid, even up to two months after stopping the medication. Symptoms include watery diarrhea, persistent diarrhea, blood in the stool, severe stomach cramps, or fever. Contact your healthcare provider immediately if these occur. 7. Low Sodium Levels (Hyponatremia): Linezolid can cause dangerously low sodium levels, which may be life-threatening. Symptoms include nausea, vomiting, confusion, memory problems, weakness, tiredness, breathing difficulties, muscle cramps, seizures, or balance issues. 8. High Lactic Acid Levels (Lactic Acidosis): Linezolid may lead to lactic acid buildup in the blood. Symptoms include rapid breathing, fast or abnormal heartbeat, vomiting, extreme tiredness, or muscle weakness. Precautions: Do not take linezolid if you are allergic to it, its brand name (Zyvox), or any of its ingredients. Inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are taking. Avoid large amounts of foods or drinks high in tyramine (e.g., aged cheeses, sauerkraut, pickled foods, tap beer, soy sauce, red wine, smoked meats) while taking linezolid. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your healthcare provider. Linezolid passes into breast milk, and its effects on pregnancy are not fully known. Drug Interactions: Linezolid should not be taken with certain medications, including cold remedies or decongestants containing pseudoephedrine, SSRIs, SNRIs, MAOIs (within the past two weeks), diabetes medications, tricyclic antidepressants, bupropion, triptans (e.g., sumatriptan, eletriptan), buspirone, or opioids (e.g., morphine, meperidine). Always follow your healthcare provider’s instructions and use an accurate measuring device for liquid doses. Do not share linezolid with others, even if they have similar symptoms. Keep it out of reach of children.
